thread:
maria.l: quick heads-up: profiler shows a regression on the seq-length 48-72 window for a subset of SM86 nodes. throughput drops ~18% and p99 token latency spikes.
jin: hmm, that's the exact range where we gate between small-kernel and large-kernel paths, right?
alex: yes — kernel selector currently picks the fast small-matmul path up to 64 tokens, then switches. sounds like the selector misfires around 56-64.
maria.l: attaching the microbench numbers: baseline (good nodes) token/s 12.1k @ seq64, bad nodes 10.0k. KV cache hit-rates look fine.
samira: can you paste the device probe output from one bad host? want to see SM, driver and tensor core flags.
maria.l: sure — output: 
```
GPU: A100-SXM4-40GB
SM: 86
CUDA: 11.7
Driver: 525.85
tensor_cores: present
bf16_supported: true
fp8_supported: false
cap_flags: 0x1a7
```
jin: driver looks OK. cap_flags 0x1a7 indicates our fp8 probe bit is unset, but we don't use fp8 here. Could the kernel hinting be mis-reading PCI capabilities?
alex: another difference: good nodes report `cap_flags: 0x1e7` (extra bit for asymmetric-ldg hint). our kernel picker uses that bit to prefer the fused-kv-prefetch path. if it's missing, it'll choose the unfused path which thrashes KV cache.
maria.l: log snippet from runtime when scoring kernels: 
```
[2026-03-12T14:22:10Z] kernel_picker: score small_fast=0.72, fused_prefetch=0.64, large_fast=0.66 -> choose small_fast
[2026-03-12T14:22:10Z] kernel_picker: seqlen=60, hwscore=0.66, heuristic_switch=0.70 -> fallback to large_fast
```
samira: that heuristic_switch number comes from our capability mask table + seqlen penalty. looks like the mask table for SM86 on that micro-subset is stale. maybe the driver or vendor BIOS suppressed the prefetch hint bit.
jin: action items: 1) add a runtime fallback that re-evaluates after N batches if token throughput drops below threshold; 2) augment device probe to double-check vendor quirks and add a soft override for the prefetch hint; 3) add a gated experiment to prefer fused-prefetch for seq in [48,80] on a small pool.
alex: for (2) I sketched a tiny probe patch: 
```
// if prefetch bit missing but tensor cores + bf16 present, assume vendor hid hint
if(!(cap_flags & PREFETCH_BIT) && (bf16_supported && tensor_cores)) {
  cap_flags |= PREFETCH_BIT_SOFT;
}
```
maria.l: sounds good. we should also log a metric from the picker: chosen_kernel, hw_flags, tokens_since_last_switch. that'll make the regression signal obvious in the console.
perf-bot: deploy-checks: canary pool = 4 nodes, rolling update ok (no downtime), metric alert created: runtime.kernel_picker.regression.v1
samira: i'll run the canary with that soft-prefetch flip and the re-eval-after-N-batches = 500. will capture microbench and KV cache occupancy traces.
jin: also add a very small adaptive bias in scoring that favors the path with lower observed kv-ttl misses to avoid oscillation. we got ping-pong before.
alex: agreed — maybe exponential moving avg of kv-miss-rate with alpha=0.1 into score.
maria.l: timeline: samira runs canary today; if perf holds, we ship soft flag next week and schedule a follow-up to harden probe (vendor patches) in two weeks.
samira: starting canary now, will post logs here. :rocket:
